issue_context.title: Apiserver panics creating a stateful set
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Apiserver panics creating a stateful set which is invalid semantically but valid json-wise according to godoc.

**What you expected to happen**:
Apiserver rejects the create request with a validation error.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Add the following lines to [this stateful set example](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/#components) and apply it
```
  updateStrategy:
    type: OnDelete
    rollingUpdate: {}
``` 
observe the internal error message from apiserver
```
error: error when creating "stateful.yaml": Post https://localhost:6443/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/default/statefulsets: stream error: stream ID 73; INTERNAL_ERROR
```
see the panic message in apiserver log
```
Observed a panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```
OTOH, use the following `updateStrategy` will result in a validation error as expected
```
  updateStrategy:
    type: OnDelete
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 0
```
apiserver response:
```
The StatefulSet "web" is invalid: spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate: Invalid value: apps.RollingUpdateStatefulSetStrategy{Partition:0}: only allowed for updateStrategy 'RollingUpdate'
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
The nil pointer deref comes from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f4521bf5a21865738f49a1c73e6aa75200a99240/pkg/apis/apps/v1/conversion.go#L438

`Partition` was nil because the defaulting only applies when `updateStrategy` is of rolling update type. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f4521bf5a21865738f49a1c73e6aa75200a99240/pkg/apis/apps/v1/defaults.go#L110

I feel the defaulting should happen regardless of the update strategy type, so that apiserver will be able to decode the request payload instead of panicking. Apiserver will be able to reject the request with a validation error as expected. 

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): HEAD

/assign
/sig apps

review_comments:
`spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate` should be unset if `spec.updateStartegy` isn't `RollingUpdate`, ref #35345

Is it not possible to leave it unset?

> `spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate` should be unset if `spec.updateStartegy` isn't `RollingUpdate`

yes, this rule is enforced during validation. This PR changes the following behavior:

If `spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate` is set and `spec.updateStartegy` isn't `RollingUpdate`, e.g. 
```
  updateStrategy:
    type: OnDelete
    rollingUpdate: {}
```

- before this change, apiserver panics during conversion and the client sees a 500 internal server error
- after this change, apiserver rejects during validation and the client sees the validation error

ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/81616 for more info. Alternatively we can fix the conversion function, but changing the defaulting seems more aligned with the godoc

> Alternatively we can fix the conversion function, but changing the defaulting seems more aligned with the godoc

IMO current defaulting behavior is aligned with godoc, which states that `rollingUpdate` is only used by the type is `RollingUpdate`:

```
// RollingUpdate is used to communicate parameters when Type is RollingUpdateStatefulSetStrategyType.
```

Note that changing defaults is breaking. This may trigger a (surprising and unwanted) rolling update to users' StatefulSets when they upgrade their clusters. 

It'd be safer & compatible to fix conversion instead. Also, would you add a test to catch the API server panic issue? Thanks!

@janetkuo Thanks for the suggestion! It turns out that the conversion has been fixed by 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82780. The current conversion code (auto-generated) handles `*int -> int` conversion properly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5e31799701123c50025567b8534e1a62dbc0e9f6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/conversion.go#L49-L52

I tested locally and the panic issue is gone

/close
